turns.input: *He asks Hadrik Voss who they think he is and where he comes from.*
turns.narration:
Hadrik Voss turns from the square's edge, the small rectangular lenses still resting on his nose from whatever he'd been examining. He looks Nicco up and down—taking in the height, the weight, the unfamiliar face and the few white hairs catching the daylight—before answering.

"You're someone I've never seen before in a part of the city where strangers stand out," he says. "Tall build, no accent I can place, asking strange questions of a dwarf he doesn't know. That tells me what you are: new here, and maybe new everywhere." He shrugs his broad shoulders, the motion barely disturbing the tools clustered at his belt. "Where you come from? Couldn't say. Somewhere that doesn't make men like you. Beyond that, you'd have to tell me yourself, and I don't expect you will." His dry tone suggests he isn't waiting for an answer. "I'm Hadrik Voss. I fix things that break. You standing in Heartstone Square with questions means you're either lost, hopeful, or you've business with the tower. Which is your concern, not mine, unless you've metalwork needs."

[CHARACTER KNOWLEDGE ACCESS]
Facts: F1 campaign_fact_nicco_light_mage "Nicco is a Light mage." | F2 campaign_fact_nicco_otherworlder "Nicco came to this world from another world." | H1 household "Nicco is owner of the household Heartstone."
Narration and Nicco (player): F1, F2, H1. Nicco's speech and decisions still belong to the player.
Hadrik Voss: CAN USE none; DO NOT USE F1, F2, H1
A character may voice or act on only the facts listed CAN USE for them (believes/suspects/heard_rumor: only as belief, suspicion or rumor). DO NOT USE also covers hints, rumors, "everyone says" talk and claims that imply the fact; do not invent rumors or public talk to get around it. DO NOT USE is this turn's permission, not proof of ignorance: that character may ask, say they have not heard, or defer to someone who can use it.
UNKNOWN IS NOT A RUMOR: when a character cannot use a fact, it is unknown to them, never something they heard. "People say", "I heard", "word is", "everyone knows", registries, records, reports, past meetings or sightings are sources; a character may cite one only when a CAN USE entry with that basis exists. Allowed instead: "I don't know", a question, or a guess explicitly framed as a guess and based only on what they can see or hear right now.
